# Turning “That doesn’t seem right” into evidence

**Ryohei Yamamoto (Kobayashi), MD, PhD**<br>
I draw on clinical experience in emergency and intensive care medicine and training in clinical epidemiology to turn questions from everyday practice into testable research. As a Visiting Scientist at the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology, I study bias and fairness in medical AI, the transportability of prediction models, and causal inference using real-world data.

[Explore my research](research.qmd){.btn .btn-primary} [GitHub](https://github.com/ryohei-hey){.btn .btn-outline-dark}
:::
:::

::: {.home-grid}
::: {.home-intro}
## About

I am a board-certified specialist in emergency and intensive care medicine, hold a PhD in medicine, and am a certified expert of the Society for Clinical Epidemiology. Through study design, observational data analysis, and prediction model evaluation, I aim to clarify what findings mean, for whom, and under which conditions.

This website brings together my research, publications, open projects, and educational resources.
:::

::: {.principles}
### Focus

**Clinical epidemiology**  
I translate clinical questions into testable research questions and well-defined estimands.

**Critical care**  
I study treatment in critical care and long-term, patient-centered outcomes.

**Causal inference**  
I emphasize assumptions, limitations, and reproducibility in causal inference from observational data.

**AI bias & fairness**<br>
I examine whether medical AI produces less equitable predictions across hospitals and patient populations.
:::
:::
